newsitem.title: USA: Foundation, Health Systems to merge.
newsitem.headline: Foundation, Health Systems to merge.

text.p: Foundation Health Corp and Health Systems International Inc said Tuesday they have a definitive agreement to combine in a merger-of-equals.
The deal is valued at about $3 billion, based on the companies' combined market capitalization, the companies said.

The merger calls for Foundation to become a subsidiary of Health Systems, and for Health Systems to change its name to Foundation Health Systems Inc. The new entity is expected to have revenues exceeding $8 billion fiscal 1997, the companies said.

Foundation stockholders will get 1.3 Foundation Health Systems Class A common shares for each Foundation share. Outstanding Health Systems Class A common shares will remain outstanding pursuant to the agreement and will become an equivalent number of Foundation Health Systems Class A common shares, the companies said.
The California Wellness Foundation, which owns 19.3 million shares of Class B non-voting Health Systems stock, will hold the same number of Class B non-voting shares of the new company.
The new company will have about 124 million shares outstanding, 61 percent of which will be owned by Foundation stockholders and 39 percent by Health Systems stockholders, the companies said.

Foundation Chairman, President and Chief Executive Daniel Crowley will remain chairman for a year after the merger and serve as a company director thereafter. Health Systems Chairman and Chief Executive Malik Hasan will be the new company's president and chief executive officer and become chairman after Crowley leaves the post, the companies said.
The merger will be a tax-free, pooling of interests and should be completed by the end of January 1997.

The new company's board will have 11 members, including Crowley, Hasan and nine independent directors. Foundation will chose five of these directors and Health Systems will chose four, the companies said.
